question_text: A security team must guarantee that NO account in specific organizational units can invoke Bedrock models outside approved Regions — a guardrail that even account administrators cannot override. Which AWS Organizations feature enforces this?

options.text: Service Control Policies (SCPs) applied to the target OUs
An IAM role in each account

explanation: SCPs in AWS Organizations set the maximum permissions boundary for accounts/OUs; a deny SCP on out-of-Region Bedrock calls cannot be overridden by account admins. An IAM role only grants within one account and can be changed locally; a Cognito policy governs app users, not account-wide service use; Security Groups filter network traffic, not API authorization.
source_topic: Service Control Policies for org-wide Bedrock restriction

topic: AWS Control Tower for governed multi-account
question_text: An enterprise standing up many AWS accounts for different GenAI teams wants a managed landing zone that applies baseline guardrails, account provisioning, and centralized governance out of the box. Which service provides this?
explanation: AWS Control Tower sets up and governs a secure multi-account landing zone with automated account provisioning and preventive/detective guardrails built on Organizations, Config, and other services. AWS Config alone tracks resource compliance but is not a full landing-zone framework; Bedrock Guardrails is model-level content safety; X-Ray is distributed tracing.
source_topic: AWS Control Tower landing zone governance

topic: Continuous config compliance with AWS Config
question_text: A governance team needs to continuously detect when GenAI-related resources drift out of compliance — e.g. a Bedrock invocation-logging setting disabled or an S3 bucket made public — and record a history of configuration changes. Which service provides this?

options.text: AWS Config with config rules and configuration history

explanation: AWS Config records resource configurations over time and evaluates them against config rules, flagging drift/non-compliance (e.g. disabled logging, public buckets). CloudFront is a CDN, Secrets Manager stores secrets, and Polly is text-to-speech — none perform configuration compliance evaluation.

topic: Audit evidence collection with Audit Manager
question_text: To prepare for an external audit of a GenAI platform, a compliance team wants to automatically collect evidence and map it to a framework's controls on an ongoing basis. Which AWS service is purpose-built for this?
explanation: AWS Audit Manager continuously collects evidence and maps it to controls in frameworks (e.g. SOC 2, HIPAA), streamlining audit preparation. Trusted Advisor gives best-practice checks, Inspector scans for vulnerabilities, and Budgets tracks cost/usage thresholds — none automate audit evidence-to-control mapping.
source_topic: AWS Audit Manager for audit evidence

topic: Secrets Manager for external API keys
question_text: A GenAI integration calls a third-party API and must store that API key securely with automatic rotation and audited, IAM-controlled retrieval — not hard-coded in code or environment variables. Which service should hold the key?

options.text: A plaintext value in a Lambda environment variable
A comment in the application source code

explanation: AWS Secrets Manager stores secrets encrypted, supports automatic rotation, and gates retrieval via IAM with CloudTrail auditing — the correct home for third-party API keys. Lambda env vars, unencrypted S3 objects, and source-code comments all expose the secret and lack rotation and fine-grained auditing.
source_topic: AWS Secrets Manager for third-party API keys
